scenarios.name: Practice starts from an isolated day copy and keeps its declared case, SAN and unique instance authority
F12 completes through actual shelf pickup and four casts, consuming time and passive resources exactly once
F13 completes with the same actual carried crate and a closed functional registered freezer at zero stamina
An actual enemy hit changes all SAN copies once and records only one first-hit minor injury
Paused action, pursuit, panic, coffee and resource clocks all remain frozen
A real preparation coffee debt crossing into a practice settles once at its actual due minute
Initial zero SAN can stabilize while really walking, then finish F13 without an invented recovery receipt
Only actual started work interrupts portable stabilization; an invalid distant action does not
Zero SAN without a recovery ends at the real panic deadline and stops all modules at that instant
A real eight-second stabilization ending at the panic deadline succeeds without adding a hidden frame
Starting stabilization genuinely 0.01 seconds too late cannot borrow time beyond the panic deadline
An actual verified mint restores all SAN copies once and cannot be consumed or credited twice
Unknown food and supplies needing their own world action cannot be used as instant practice recovery
Actual store completion at an attack endpoint wins before that same-frame hit is applied
Objective completion with newly due zero-SAN debt stays active until real stabilization finishes
Completing, re-entering pause and repeated ticking never mints a second terminal result or campaign reward
An unavailable world setup never advances any of the three clocks or consumes the day inventory
Cancelling an actual store retains the original meat and cannot complete either the encounter or exercise

scope: Integrated isolated F12/F13 practice with actual world movement/actions, synchronized SAN and panic, exact dated resource debt and no campaign reward writes. Does not prove a full six-wave night, all monsters, mobile UI, production persistence or arbitrary simultaneous events.
